request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [Redacted]

Date of Admission: [Redacted]

Date of Discharge: [Redacted]

Reason for Admission:
The patient was admitted due to dizziness, fatigue, and increasing abdominal distension.

Hospital Course:
During the hospital stay, the patient was found to have anemia, hypoalbuminemia, and renal failure. Tumor markers were within normal range. A CT scan revealed an extremely large mass occupying most of the abdomen and pelvis, which was ultimately diagnosed as type 1 papillary RCC with nuclear grade 2. The mass was resected after dissecting it free from its attachments. A perforated anterior duodenal ulcer was also noted and repaired. The patient developed intra-abdominal abscess and required drainage and antibiotics in the intensive care unit. Due to ongoing deterioration, comfort care measures were initiated and the patient deceased 1 month later.
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment During Hospital Stay:
The patient was started on enteral feeds and underwent surgery for resection of the mass and repair of a perforated anterior duodenal ulcer. The patient also received antibiotics and pressors during the hospital stay.

Follow-up:
The patient is deceased and requires no further follow-up.

Discharge Medications:
N/A

Discharge Condition:
Deceased.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The principal diagnosis is malignant neoplasm of the kidney, category C64.

- **Condition chiefly responsible for the admission:** The patient presented with dizziness, fatigue and abdominal distension. Investigation found a very large abdominal and pelvic mass. It was diagnosed as type 1 papillary renal cell carcinoma, and it was the main target of treatment (surgical resection).
- **Chapter:** A malignant neoplasm falls under letter **C**.
- **Category:** A malignant neoplasm of the kidney, other than the renal pelvis, is **C64**. Papillary renal cell carcinoma arises in the kidney itself, so it belongs here.
- **Why not the other conditions:**
  - The anaemia, hypoalbuminaemia and renal failure were findings that accompanied the tumour.
  - The perforated duodenal ulcer (K26) was found during surgery and repaired, so it is a secondary diagnosis.
  - The intra-abdominal abscess was a later complication of the stay.

CODE: C64
